messages.author: 85d768b545989d80
messages.subject: Running knitr in parallel.
parts:
I want to speed up the generation of reports by running several knit2pdf in parallel. I have a master Rnw-document that also run knit_child in a loop. I have the knit2pdf inside a small R.file that I run with RScript from console (Ubuntu).

It works fine to run one report-generation at a time, but when i start to generate a second report while the first report-generation is still running, then I get "Error in createLockFile(lockname) : cannot create lock file" because knitr needs to create the files abc-tikzDictionary and abc-tikzDictionary___LOCK (abc is the name of my child-Rnw file).

Is there a way to make knitr use different file-names for the tikzDictionary per report-generation run, so there will be no lock-conflict?

Thanks.

/Chris

messages.author: 586344112c6002f7
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Running knitr in parallel.
parts:
I want to respond to this question as it seemed like it would be good to keep threads on this topic together. I am working on large scale report generation in knitr where at any one time I could be generating hundreds of reports based off of various geographies in a large scale database. The reports individually take about 5 minutes to run. If I wanted to run a report on every county in the US that is about 3,000 counties in total. 

I am using a method not unsimilar to this one here:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/15396755/using-loops-with-knitr-to-produce-multiple-pdf-reports-need-a-little-help-to

Basically you loop through a Rnw file (document class is report in LaTex) to create many different pdfs.

library("knitr")
for (hosp in unique(df$Hospital)){
  knit2pdf("testingloops.Rnw", output=paste0('report_', hosp, '.tex'))
}
Generally I'm querying the relational database a bunch and drawing maps, plots, xtables, etc.

I tried simply replacing the for loop with a foreach loop (and executing via %dopar%) based on a doMC parallel backend. This process seems to work very slowly mostly because I think it is gathering the results and communicating them back to the original R file. So something like this:

library("knitr")
foreach (i=1:nrow(unique(df$County)){
  knit2pdf("testingloops.Rnw", output=paste0('report_', unique(df$County)[i], '.tex'))
}
I'm wondering:

1. Is it even worth it to actually parallelize the reports or just to run the loops as chunks on different machines
2. Am I not using some of the foreach combine arguments correctly.

This question I think is unique. I'm not really trying to do parallel computation inside a knitr document. I am trying to parallelize teh creation of many knitr documents. Does this make sense?

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Running knitr in parallel.
parts:
But... this actually is not the same topic, since the original message had nothing about foreach, and it was knitting a single report together.

Regardless, parallel processing is not a panacea for making things go faster... it is targeted at things that need more cpu specifically. Having multiple processes fighting over I/O resources (database access, filesystem access, graphics device access, RAM access) is not a good way to speed things up. If your reports take a lot of cpu time and not too much RAM then you might get a boost, but it doesn't sound like that is the case for you. Even switching to using only one process per machine might not help if network access to your database is saturated. Profiling the generation of one report might be useful for understanding what you are up against.
